Definition: to drive out from a possession; especially to expatriate or divorce
BiblicalUsage: Garash means to drive out from a possession, to expel — and it is used for nations, priests, and men alike. God drove out nations before His people in 1 Chronicles 17:21, and Solomon thrust out Abiathar from the priesthood in 1 Kings 2:27. David says the children of men have driven him out from abiding in the inheritance of the LORD in 1 Samuel 26:19, and the enemies of Judah would cast them out of their possession in 2 Chronicles 20:11.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe driving out is God's judgment and man's cruelty in the same word. God drives out nations to give His people a home, and men drive out David to take his home away. I hold that the inheritance God gives cannot be taken by men.
